Drive for Uber? You owe GST from your very first ride. There's no thirty thousand dollar pass.
CRA says commercial ride-sharing drivers must register for GST, even as small suppliers.
Deliver food only, for DoorDash? Different rule: you register once sales pass thirty thousand.
Our Manitoba driver takes in twenty thousand in fares. The GST is usually already inside the fare.
Five over one hundred five. About nine hundred fifty-two dollars of that belongs to CRA.
But the GST you paid on gas and repairs for the rides comes back. Here, two hundred dollars.
Insurance and loan interest? No GST credit there.
So about seven fifty-two goes to CRA. The same twenty thousand, delivering food only: no GST registration required.
